_activity: From a 4 to a 5: context for 1786
_licence: ORIGINAL, built on the 11.2 casefile documents (numbered per the signed 11.2 map). Quotes are the casefile's adapted text.
design_intent: Not skill practice. A kid here already writes at a 4. This is the gold dust that turns a 4 into a 5: more content, a wider lens, and a named technique.

tidbits.text: Daniel Shays was a Continental Army veteran. Many of the rebels had fought in the Revolution and came home to debts and taxes they couldn't pay.
tidbits.thread: Thread 3 — The Role and Size of Government
tidbits.source_pointer: Casefile B, Day 7 WHAT YOU NEED TO KNOW; wider-lens detail

tidbits.text: Washington had retired to Mount Vernon. Shays' Rebellion helped convince him to come to Philadelphia in 1787, where he presided over the Convention.
The Threads card's question for this era: “Can a government be too weak to protect democracy — just as it can be too strong?” Context for 1786 is the “too weak” half of that question.

exemplars.text: In 1786, farmers in Massachusetts rebelled, and the government under the Articles couldn't stop them, which is why Washington was worried.

In the late summer and fall of 1786, just ten years after declaring independence from a king with too much power, Americans were living under a national government with too little: Congress had no money and could not pay for an army, so when debt-ridden farmers shut down Massachusetts courts, only a privately funded army could stop them, which is why Washington warned Madison the country was heading toward ruin.
exemplars.what_changed: The 4 names the event. The 5 reaches back to 1776 and names the swing from too much power to too little, so the context explains the whole problem, not just one rebellion.

techniques.name: Reach-back
techniques.explanation: Name one earlier moment that explains how things got here. Here, 1776 explains why the Articles were weak on purpose.

techniques.name: Name the swing
techniques.explanation: Say what the country was swinging from and to: too much power, then too little. It shows you see the pattern.

try_it.prompt: Washington worried a government could be too weak to protect people. When have you seen a group (a team, a club, a class) struggle because nobody had the power to make a decision stick?
try_it.status: Untimed, optional, never scored, never saved — practice reflection only.
